## Review Fast Path

- Observable claim + acceptance criteria: Jarvis behavior PRs cannot enter tester or release ownership without an explicit proof-layer receipt; local-only evidence cannot claim consumer shipment, and product delivery claims fail when required source, package, runtime, migration, release, or end-user receipts are missing.
- Exact head + builder proof: `c69952329cc571d718d635e4a18208f26a6fb59e`; 3 focused files / 79 tests passed, type-aware lint passed, formatting and syntax passed.
- Independent tester: Pending exact-head lifecycle handoff.
- Jarvis delivery boundary: Product-wide governance, source boundary complete; receipt below.
- Release worker: Pending exact-head tester PASS and fenced queue handoff.
- Dependencies / merge order / overlap: None — standalone. The concurrent personal-skill migration owns runtime/onboarding files and confirmed no overlap with this governance write set.
- Remaining proof / cleanup / rollback: Required CI, independent tester, and source merge remain. No Jarvis.app package, install, runtime, migration, or public release is applicable to this governance-only source change. Roll back with one revert.
- Still hurts: A deliberately mislabeled PR that omits Jarvis from its title, claim text, and direct product paths can evade mechanical detection; repository agent policy still requires classification.

## Why This Matters

- A personal Jarvis customization was previously mistaken for consumer delivery.
- Source, package, installed runtime, upgrade adoption, public release, and end-user behavior are separate states and must stay separate in every future Jarvis task.
- One receipt now carries that truth through CI, builder-to-tester handoff, and the fenced release queue.
